name: The Diadem
holds: the rift peninsula, the Cindered Plains (occupied)
stance_on_the_war: war victor; claims the whole inheritance
condition: small, dry, damaged; feeding it is the entire Act 1 problem
naval_posture: THE SEA POWER: war galleys out of Thessala, warm water, year-round; a fire weapon nobody else has and nobody else understands
comparative_advantage: reach -- it can feed itself from anywhere with a coast

name: The Assembly
holds: the taiga belt and the forest lakes
stance_on_the_war: war victor; calls the Diadem a crown worn by whoever survived
condition: CONSTITUTIONAL COLLAPSE, not just resource-poor: legitimacy runs on assent of the great houses, and enough house heads died in the plague that Vetch may not currently have quorum to seat a government at all -- a rump council improvising rather than a functioning state. A crisis of authority, distinct from the Diadem's crisis of resources; this asymmetry was present in the original FE3H-era design (plague-and-no-spiritual-relief vs. crops-destroyed) and thinned out in the de-pivot -- restored here on purpose, since it primes which of the two Act 3 threats makes sense before the player ever chooses.
naval_posture: no fleet and no shipwrights; Halder ices shut a third of the year
comparative_advantage: interior lines, timber, horses -- and credit: it HIRES fleets it cannot build

name: The Toll League
constitution: no sovereign; three cities, one treaty
holds: the caravan road and its oases
stance_on_the_war: neutral by policy, because both sides must pay to eat
condition: the Company's power base; grace as circulating credit is THEIR doctrine
naval_posture: none; the League is a road, not a coast
comparative_advantage: the only gap in the mountain wall, and it charges for it

name: The River Kingdoms
holds: the eastern river valley and delta
stance_on_the_war: indifferent; both successor states are provincial to them
condition: oldest continuous cities on the map; the lending houses; where learning comes from
naval_posture: river craft only, but they finance everyone else's ships
comparative_advantage: capital, and the oldest continuous records on the map

name: The Herd Clans
stance_on_the_war: the Assembly's elective constitution came from here, which the Diadem calls proof of barbarism
condition: cannot be conquered because there is nothing to seize
comparative_advantage: cannot be conquered because there is nothing to seize

name: The Green Ports
stance_on_the_war: sells grain to anyone; the Diadem's fleet goes here
condition: wet, rich, and entirely uninterested in the war
naval_posture: the best merchant hulls afloat, and no navy at all
comparative_advantage: grain, and a policy of selling it to both sides

name: The Isles
condition: a hermit saint lives here and refuses to adjudicate anything
naval_posture: fishing boats that know water no chart shows
comparative_advantage: pilotage -- the Isles' crews are why anyone crosses safely
